why: The briefs do neither of the two banned things. Item 1: no verifier check uses `npm run test:cli` to decide PASS or FAIL. Check 6 runs `npm test; echo "exit=$?"` and then the grep. `test:cli` comes up only under "Advisory (none of this affects PASS or FAIL)", which notes that the script doesn't exist. Item 2: the builder brief never asks for a general separator option. It does the opposite, saying "do not add --help, --sep/--delimiter, auto-detection or quoting rules". It asks only for a `--tsv` flag that calls `parse(text, '\t')`. The verifier brief also lists `--sep` as something to note if it shows up outside the non-goals. One line in builder step 3 is garbled (`[{"a\\tb":"1\\tb"...`), but that is a quality problem, not a must_not breach.
